summary.title: Faster Base64 Encoding and Decoding Using AVX2 Instructions
summary.one_liner: SIMD (AVX2) techniques can make base64 encoding about 10x and decoding about 7x faster than prior state-of-the-art implementations while still rejecting invalid characters.
takeaways: Base64 is widely used to embed images, fonts, and other resources in HTML, JavaScript, JSON, and XML, and billions of messages are decoded daily according to the authors.
Using AVX2 SIMD instructions on recent Intel processors, the authors report roughly 10x faster encoding and 7x faster decoding versus state-of-the-art implementations.
The accelerated software follows the base64 specification and reports errors on characters outside the base64 alphabet.
The implementation is released as free software under a liberal license.
summary.summary: This arXiv paper (Lemire and coauthors, first submitted 2017, revised 2026) argues that base64 conversion is worth speeding up because it is used so widely on the web. It describes using AVX2 SIMD instructions on Intel processors to process many bytes at once for both encoding and decoding. The abstract reports roughly 10x faster encoding and 7x faster decoding than prior implementations, and says the code follows the spec and flags invalid characters. The page text shown is the abstract and arXiv metadata only, so the technical method details are not visible here.
